clue.text: They tend to bring up unrelated issues

definitions.text: They tend to bring up unrelated issues

parts.words: They tend to bring up unrelated issues
parts.note: issues are offspring, and those who raise children not born to them are carers by arrangement rather than blood

explanation.surface: People who habitually raise topics that have nothing to do with the matter in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' reads as mentioning, and 'issues' as topics; in fact they mean raising children who are not one's own.
explanation.definitionFit: Carers who raise children not related to them by birth are exactly those who rear unrelated offspring.

clue.text: One may hear it from a Liberal or a Conservative

definitions.text: One may hear it from a Liberal

parts.note: taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Speech-making is what you get from politicians of either main party.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquent public speaking is what audiences hear from any politician, Liberal included.

clue.text: Dog-end

definitions.meaning: to dog someone is to follow them closely, to shadow them
the rear end or hindmost part of an animal or thing

explanation.definitionFit: Shadowing someone and the rear part are both senses of the same short word.

clue.text: Rushed to fire rifle

parts.note: rushed means ran
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: A soldier hurried to discharge his gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it roughly while stealing, a synonym of plunder.

clue.text: A rise for the workers?

parts.note: a rise is a small mound, and worker insects build one as their nest

explanation.surface: A pay increase for the labour force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' suggests a pay increase and 'workers' employees; here the workers are insects and the rise is their mound.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker insects heap earth into a small hill as their colony's home, a literal raised mound.

clue.text: A high-flier of merit on the phone

indicators.note: a word heard over the phone is identified only by its sound

parts.note: to merit something is to earn it

explanation.surface: A successful achiever with distinction talking on the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle soars high, so it is literally a high-flying bird; crossword setters love it.

clue.text: Accommodation for spectators in Chester racecourse …

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words Chester racecourse, spanning the join

explanation.surface: Seating for racegoers at the course in Chester.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepped standing area at a sports ground houses watching crowds.

clue.text: … where one aims for this last job

parts.note: the last of something is its finishing part
a job is a post

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: at the racecourse, a final task.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the racecourse in the previous clue, which is where runners aim for this.
explanation.definitionFit: Racehorses and runners aim to reach the marker at the end of the course.

clue.text: Take-off for country after breaking promise

indicators.note: the country comes after the rearranged letters
a promise that is broken is smashed up, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: A state breaks its word.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a comic mimicry of someone, a satirical copy of their manner.

clue.text: Foreigner, one with a Latin derivation, perhaps

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: a derivation is something formed out of other material, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A person from abroad whose language comes from Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Italy is a foreigner to a British reader, an example of the category.

clue.text: A bad-tempered pet

parts.note: a pet can be a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet', not only a domestic animal

explanation.surface: A grumpy household animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' suggests a cat or dog, but an old sense is a fit of peevishness.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of childish rage is a bad-tempered outburst, an old sense of a pet.

clue.text: Smooth metal

definitions.meaning: to smooth creases from clothes with a heated appliance
the element Fe, a common metal

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes flat and the element Fe share one name.

clue.text: Costume that's hard to get out of

definitions.meaning: a monk's or nun's robe, or riding dress

definitions.text: that's hard to get out of
definitions.meaning: an ingrained custom, difficult to break

explanation.definitionFit: A religious garment and an ingrained routine are both called by this word.

clue.text: Punishment for a murderer pronounced

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the name is matched by its sound

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in the Book of Genesis

explanation.surface: The penalty a killer deserves, it is declared.
explanation.walkthrough: Cain is the Bible's first murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating with a stick was a school punishment in Britain until the 1980s.

clue.text: One in conspiracy to control the ship

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the word for a conspiracy

parts.note: a conspiracy is a plot
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A mutineer plots to take over the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer a vessel through difficult waters is to guide or control it.

clue.text: Part of unit fuming to be sent back in plain clothes

indicators.note: sending something back returns it, so the stretch is read in the other direction
only a stretch of the words unit fuming is used

explanation.surface: A section of an angry military unit is returned out of uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Civilian dress worn by someone, such as a soldier, who usually wears uniform.

clue.text: Stack of food the farmer may plunge his fork into

definitions.text: Stack of food the farmer may plunge his fork into

parts.words: Stack of food the farmer may plunge his fork into
parts.note: a pile of fodder that a farmer forks, not a plate of food eaten with a fork

explanation.surface: A heaped plate a hungry farmer digs into at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food' and 'fork' suggest a meal; the fork is a pitchfork and the food is animal fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A stacked heap of dried grass is cattle feed that farmers pitch with forks.

clue.text: Bays of victory

parts.note: bay leaves were woven into wreaths for winners in ancient Greece

explanation.surface: Inlets named after triumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bays' suggests coastal inlets; it means bay trees, whose leaves crowned victors.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay trees provided the wreaths crowning winners, so the plant stands for honours won.

clue.text: Contracts for Polar missiles?

parts.note: N is north, a polar direction
arrows are missiles

explanation.surface: Agreements to supply weapons to the Arctic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that contracts becomes thinner, getting tighter or less wide.

clue.text: Cases prepared for Italian consumer groups

definitions.text: Cases prepared for Italian consumer groups

parts.words: Cases prepared for Italian consumer groups
parts.note: pasta parcels made to be eaten by Italians, served in portions, not legal cases for a consumer body

explanation.surface: Lawsuits got ready on behalf of Italy's consumer associations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' and 'consumer groups' suggest consumer law; the cases are pasta envelopes and the consumer is an eater.
explanation.definitionFit: Small filled pasta envelopes are cases cooked for eaters, a classic Italian dish.

clue.text: Showed surprise as good man's taken on new trade

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was amazed when a virtuous man took up a fresh career.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump or flinch in shock is to react with surprise.

clue.text: Sinatra, swinging expert

indicators.note: swinging means moving about, so the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra, a master of swing music.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Sinatra was an American singer known for swing.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker is an expert at a trade or craft.

clue.text: Primate swallows vegetables to satisfy hunger, perhaps

indicators.note: the primate takes the vegetables inside itself

parts.note: an ape is a primate
peas are vegetables

explanation.surface: A monkey gulps down greens to fill its stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify or relieve a craving such as hunger is to quiet or satisfy it.

clue.text: Review on thug's weapon

indicators.note: to review is to look at again, rearranging these letters

explanation.surface: A critique of a gangster's gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-bore gun firing pellets is a firearm, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Make way for pedestrians

parts.note: make way means build a path rather than step aside

explanation.surface: Step aside so walkers can pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make way' reads as stepping aside; here it means laying a walkway surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying flagstones creates a surfaced way such as a footpath.

clue.text: Contented to lay very quietly in dry grass

indicators.note: the musical marking goes inside the dried grass

parts.note: hay is dried grass
pp, pianissimo, means very quietly in music

explanation.surface: Satisfied to lie quietly in the hay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being contented means being pleased and satisfied with one's lot.

clue.text: Stronghold engaged in conflict, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: to have engaged in conflict is to have fought

explanation.surface: A fortress caught up in war, reportedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified military building is a stronghold.

clue.text: Hawk seen in Home Counties, going over lines

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the second

parts.note: the Home Counties around London are in the south-east of England, SE
L is line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A bird of prey spotted near London, flying above railway tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk goods is to peddle them in the street.

clue.text: Rising resort includes lake and mountains

indicators.note: the reversed resort holds the extra letter within it
in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a spa is a resort

explanation.surface: A fashionable holiday spot with a lake and peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The great European range is a set of high peaks.

clue.text: Sew lots, perhaps, despite being last to finish

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A tailor sews a great deal yet finishes behind everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The one moving at least speed finishes last.

clue.text: Staff instruction to get a move on

definitions.text: Staff instruction to get a move on

parts.words: Staff instruction to get a move on
parts.note: a staff is a musical stave, and a movement is a section of a symphony

explanation.surface: A manager ordering employees to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees; it is the musical stave, and 'move' hints at a movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempo marking on sheet music telling players to perform briskly.

clue.text: Muckspreading may be a remedial application

definitions.text: Muckspreading may be a remedial application

parts.words: Muckspreading may be a remedial application
parts.note: spreading manure fertilises farmland, and the same phrase names an emergency bandage

explanation.surface: Spreading manure can be a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: Muckspreading dresses a field with manure; the phrase also means a first-aid wound dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency bandage applied to a wound on the battlefield is a remedial application.
